newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SALARY CEILINGS IMPOSED IN STATE RUN-BANKS.
newsitem.headline: SALARY CEILINGS IMPOSED IN STATE RUN-BANKS.

text.p: The Lithuanian government has decided to impose salary limits on high ranking officials at state-run commercial banks, the government's press office said on Tuesday.

"In the banks where the state owns more than 50 percent the salaries for the chairman, his deputies and the board members shall be based on applying a coefficient to the basic monthly salary," the press office said in a statement.
It said that the coeficient for the salary of the chairman of the bank will be between 35 and 42 and for the member of the board 26-33.
The basic monthly salary in Lithuania is 95 litas.
The statement also said that if the bank operates profitably, bonuses shall paid but they shall not exceed 200 percent of the chairman's monthly salary.
The salaries of bank workers shall be decided by the councils of the banks but monthly bonuses shall not exceed 50 percent of their monthly salary, the statement said.
The government said that the salaries will have to be revised on a quarterly basis, taking into conideration the financial results of the bank.
The government said the total sum of bonuses paid shall not exceed 30 percent of the banks' net profit.
Local banking analysts say the government's intention to regulate salaries in state-run banks will will drive their most talented people into the private sector.
